rows.author: C093
rows.abstract:
Said that his home province of Cagayan despite its vast natural resources was very poor because of the way the government had defined agricultural and trade policies. Stressed that in order for the Philippines to attain food security, it must first establish its food sovereignty or its right to define its own agriculture, labor, fishing, food and land
policies which are ecologically, socially, economically and culturally appropriate to its circumstances. Urged his colleagues to support
his recommendations to prioritize agricultural
infrastructure support; ensure access to low-interest agricultural credit; remove all subsidies on export oriented agriculture and transfer the subsidies to grains and vegetable farmers and livestock growers; launch a campaign against smuggling and dumping of food and agri-based products and commodities that could be supplied by our own local producers;
reclaim our original strength on agricultural research and scientific breakthroughs; strengthen the National Food Authority as a state-trading enterprise that protects
our farmers and fisherfolks and their produce
from predatory elements; and break all land monopolies as government implements the last phase of land reform.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-12-06)

rows.author: C128
rows.abstract:
Talked about the impact of cooperatives
development in poverty alleviation by citing 1) statistics to show the prevalence and magnitude of poverty in the Philippines and abroad; 2) the millennium development goal (MDG) to reduce extreme poverty and hunger by the year 2015; 3) how the United Nations (UN) acknowledged the role of cooperatives in mitigating poverty ; and 4) the profiles and accomplishments of various types of cooperatives worldwide. Cited different cooperatives in the country which have proven to be successful instruments and strong partners of the government in uplifting the lives of the poor and the underprivileged Filipinos. Recommended that the government: 1) develop
a strategy in helping the cooperative sector; 2)
examine the role of housing cooperatives in urban
policies; 3) address micro-insurance needs; 4) cooperativize the water districts; 5) rehabilitate ailing cooperative banks; 6) formulate a strategic policy direction
for the transformation of ARCs into cooperative
models; and 7) convert electric cooperatives into
genuine cooperatives with share capital from members to establish true ownership and democratic governance.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-12-06)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Fua. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G105
rows.abstract:
Informed the Body that December, 2010, is the 60th anniversary of the Int'l Declaration
of Human Rights where the country is a signatory,
and that December 6, 2010 is also the 10th
month of imprisonment of 43 health workers who
were now known as the “Morong 43” and who now
belonged to the numerous victims of human rights
violations under the Arroyo and the Aquino administrations. Recalled that they were medical practitioners and volunteer community health workers who were illegally arrested in Morong, Rizal while rendering health services under two organizations that give medical health to areas no longer accessed by government health agencies. Disclosed that Justice Sec.Leila de Lima had already reviewed their case, and that President Benigno C. Aquino III stated
that their arrest was illegal, and that the case was forwarded to the Supreme Court. Added that more than 50 House Members had asked for the release of the Morong 43 through an advertisement published in two major newspapers, and asked her colleagues to recognize the rights of the health workers.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-12-06)

rows.author: F100
rows.abstract:
Supported the plight of “kuliglig” drivers for the following reasons: 1) Executive Order No. 16 has no legal basis because they do not violate the Clean Air Act; and 2) the ban on “kuliglig” motorcycle vehicles deprive their drivers of livelihood which should not be imposed
indiscriminately on the “kuliglig” drivers of Manila. Underscored that the main issue re:
the kuliglig drivers is the displacement of
their livelihood. Maintained that as the Representative of Bayan Muna, it is his duty to be the voice of the marginalized sectors in Congress.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-12-06)

rows.author: E022
rows.title_full: SOUGHT JUSTICE FOR THE MORONG 43
rows.abstract:
Expressed his concern about the health conditions of the 36 out of the 43 detained
health workers illegally arrested in Morong, Rizal last February, who went on hunger strike to press the Aquino Administration for their release. Narrated the defective arrest of the so-called “Morong 43” who were on a community medical training and were subjected to illegal detention and torture as they were tagged by the military as members of the New People´s
Army (NPA). Asked the government to cause the withdrawal of the case so that the court could have a basis for a release order. Enjoined his colleagues to hold a sympathy fasting in solidarity with the Morong 43´s cause for human rights, freedom and justice.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2011-01-18

rows.author: G003
rows.title_full: SOUGHT JUSTICE FOR THE MORONG 43
rows.abstract:
Focused on the outcry for the release of medical practitioners and health workers comprising the so-called Morong 43 who were arrested
in February 2010 which came not only from
several Representatives who filed a resolution thereon but also from every quarter within and outside of the country. Stressed that the President already had sufficient information on the case and had the obligation to do everything within his power to remedy a situation he judged to be unjust and illegal. Urged him to clearly show where he stood and to issue the order to file the motion for the dismissal of the case.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2011-01-18

rows.title_full: INCREASED REFORESTATION EFFORTS IN CATANDUANES
rows.abstract: Brought to the attention of the Body the paramount issue of environmental care and protection that confronts the province of Catanduanes. Urged his colleagues to join him in his crusade to protect the environment through synchronized tree planting on January 11, 2011 as a commitment to environmental protection.

rows.author: F103
rows.title_full: OVER-IMPORTATION OF MEAT AND POULTRY POSING AS A THREAT TO THE LOCAL MEAT INDUSTRY
rows.abstract:
Delved on the immediate review of the Philippine´s international trade commitments
on minimum access volume on meat and
poultry. Pointed out the impact of meat over-importation, raising concerns on the quality and safety of imported meat; and the local farmers´ lament on the losses in sales over competition from imported meat. Gave several recommendations
such as implementing stricter inspection and testing systems and using part of the Agricultural Competitiveness Enhancement Fund (ACEF) to protect local meat and poultry producers. Asked for his colleagues´ help and stressed that food security meant not only food availability and accessibility but also food safety and quality.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 2011-01-18

Paez...brought to the attention of the Body several issues... underscored the importance of addessing these issues:  the 10 distressed cooperative banks under the Prompt Corrective Action of the BSP; proposed the establishment of a P2.5 billion rehabilitation fund for these banks... and the consolidation of all the 43 cooperative banks into a single cooperative bank within five years and informed the Body of his intent to file a measure establishing rehabilitation fund.  Rep. rows.abstract: Rep. Ting cited RA 8794 - MVUC Law...its provisions on overloading in particular...; cited computations to point out that the discrepancy between delivery vehicles' actual gross weight capacity and the DPWH-mandated allowable gross weight would adversely affect the delivery of goods...; mentioned the negative consequences of the matrix of gross vehicle weights...; urged the Body to revisit the law and to prioritize the consideration of his Resolution directing the Cttee. on Transportation to clarify and inquire on the computation of maximum allowable gross vehicle weight vis-a-vis the overloading provision of the MVUC Law, and thus come up with a more acceptable mechnism of protecting the national roads and the public interest.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2012-01-24

rows.abstract: Rep. Umali alleged...that SC Chief Justice Renato Corona,... had \"tacitly imputed\" that a propaganda war has been waged against the Supreme Court...; argued that Chief Justice Corona's allusion to the House as the source ...was only a means to divert the attention of the people from the \"deplorable reputation, credibility and respectability\" of the SC justices; adverted to the pertinent Constitutional provisions,...to emphasize that the Members were within the limits of the Constitution in their commentaries against the Supreme Court; claimed that the statements of the SC Justice diminish the reputation and stature of the House, and the legislators should not allow this to happen by \"rallying to the Constitution\"
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2011-02-01

rows.author: G092
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR SUPPORT TO THE \" ORIGINAL PILIPINO MUSIC \" ( O P M )
rows.abstract:
Spoke about the sad plight of the local music industry in view of the invasion of foreign artists in the local music scene, and the suggestions of the Organisasyon ng Pilipinong
Mang-aawit (OPM) led by Mr. Ogie Alcasid on how
to develop music education among the Filipino youth and how to revive the local music industry.
Urged his colleagues to support the initiatives of the OPM, one of which is the Kulturang Lahi Inuuna Ko or KLIK movement that will soon be launched, towards the promotion of original Pilipino music
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2011-02-08

rows.author: G039
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR REFORMS IN THE SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN
rows.abstract: Described the previous elections of the Liga ng mga Barangay and the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) Federation in the City of San Juan as dirty because the City´s present SK President was won by fraud, intimidation and bribery. Lamented that the SK officials can be manipulated by their parents and by corrupt politicians to protect their interests. Informed the Body that he would be introducing reforms in the SK elections one of which is to raise the age requirement from 15 to 17 years old to 18 to 25 years old. Opined that the proposed age requirement is the legal age wherein a person has reached a certain level of maturity and capable of taking responsibilities. Stressed that the SK is only for the youth and not for their parents nor for politicians.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2011-02-08
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Fua, Magsaysay M. and Cagas. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: C045
rows.title_full: ISSUES ON THE SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN
rows.abstract:
Surmised that young leaders in Rep. Cagas´ constituency may have been getting wrong
examples from their elders. Pointed out that in
his province of Ilocos Norte, three of his sons had been elected as SK Federation presidents... because of their good moral conduct and their father´s accomplishments; people were elected because of integrity and professional qualifications; and illustrious people had been elected to national executive and judicial
positions. Stressed that the nation must harness persons aged 15 to 17 because it is at this age that they are most malleable and easily influenced. He concluded that what was wrong was not the SK system and that if the elders
would set good examples, the youth will follow suit.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2011-02-08

rows.author: G064
rows.title_full: ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PANTAWID PAMILYANG PILIPINO PROGRAM (4Ps)
rows.title_short: Conditional Cash Transfer ( C C T )program
rows.abstract: Expressed his concerns re: the implementation of the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) and its Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT)component esp. with respect to the identification of the districts to be included in the program, the role of the Members of Congress in program implementation, the identification of the program´s target beneficiaries (poorest of the poor), and the assurance that the cash benefits will really reach the target recipients. Asked the House leadership to immediately organize the Oversight Ctte. on Public Expenditures to monitor the implementation of the 4Ps CCT program, and reminded the Body of the CCT secretariat´s duty to submit to Congress a quarterly status report on said programs. Urged his colleagues to be vigilant in their respective districts and to ask their regional offices of the DSWD to regularly report to them the implementation of the government´s flagship anti-poverty program.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2011-02-15
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Magsaysay (M.).  Manifestation by Rep. Escudero. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G062
rows.title_full: ON THE ISSUES SURROUNDING THE MINING OPERATIONS IN BIAK-NA-BATO
rows.abstract:
Rose to shed light on the illegal mining activities in the historic Biak-na-Bato National
Park. Stated that...it is also his duty and privilege to set the facts straight with regard
the issue. Related how he fought for the cancellation of the mining operations of Rosemoor Mining Corporation, which was then the sole mining operator in the province, and lamented that illegal mining activities,
including the transport of marbles, have again proliferated therein. Asked that Congress conduct an investigation in aid of legislation on the transport of several expensive marbles without the necessary ore transport permit (OTP). Opined that it would take time to rebuild the image of their province, and reminded his colleagues of their task of taking care not only of the country´s natural resources, but the welfare and safety of their constituents as well.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2011-02-15
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep. Sy-Alvarado. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G092
rows.title_full: MINIMUM COMMITMENTS OF TELECOM COMPANIES IN TERMS OF BANDWIDTH CONNECTIVITY
rows.abstract:
Called the attention of the Body on the alleged “discrepancy” in the internet/bandwidth
connection speed being provided to consumers by
certain Internet Service Providers (ISPs) and telecommunications companies. Claimed that contrary to what these ISPs and Telcos had claimed in their public advertisements of maximum
internet/bandwidth connection speed, what has been provided to consumers was only “a minimum bandwidth connection speed.” Proposed to
end this “technological falsification” that has brought deplorable broadband and internet connection services and astronomical bills by having these ISPs and Telcos specify the correct minimum bandwidth/internet connection speed in their advertisements.
rows.status: Scheduled for first meeting/hearing on 2011-02-19

committee_action.meethigh: This is part of the measures taken up during the Forum on Broadband/Bandwidth of the Committee on Information Communications Technology held at MINT, McKinley Hill, Taguig City on 19 February 2011, together with HR 407, 757, 799 and 800.

rows.author: F008
rows.title_full: ETON TOWER ACCIDENT
rows.title_short: Work - Related Accidents / Violation Of Occupational Safety Hazards Law
rows.abstract:
Spoke on the unnecessary and senseless deaths of 10 construction workers at the Eton Towers in Makati and those employed under hazardous conditions. Underscored the need to amend
labor laws, particularly on industrial safety. Cited that it had been practiced more for the benefit of government inspectors than in the actual compliance of mandated safety procedures. Claimed that the risk that the workers had to contend with if only to bring additional profits to their employers in terms of reduction in operational expenses and working time is a contravention of the Constitution which commands the State to afford full protection to labor. Appealed to all agencies of government, particularly the Department of Labor and Employment, to be more vigilant in the implementation, regulation and monitoring of safety standards, to provide for stricter criminal penalties and steeper fines to employers, and to provide substantial recompense
or damages awarded to the families of the victims. Maintained that government can put a stop to the continued exploitation of workers by ensuring their protection, their dignity and the welfare of their families.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2011-02-15

rows.author: G009
rows.title_full: LABOR'S INADEQUATE ACCESS TO JUSTICE
rows.abstract:
Brought to the attention of the Body the issue on the workers´ inadequate access to justice. Cited the case of the Hong Kong Shanghai Banking Corporation (HSBC) workers who were dismissed from their jobs in 1993 but up to the present, their case has not yet been resolved...; and the 1997 retrenchment case filed by the cabin crew´s union against the Phil. Airlines which was also
pending before the Supreme Court. Opined that the delay in the administration of justice erodes the society´s primordial confidence in the justice system because even a fair and just judgment
is drained of its value if rendered with undue
delay. Sought a reevaluation of the access to justice by the labor sector, particularly
that of the HSBC workers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY since 2011-02-15

rows.author: E022
rows.title_full: PLIGHT OF DISTRESSED OFWs IN SAUDI ARABIA
rows.title_short: Stranded Overseas Filipino Workers In Jeddah
rows.abstract:
Informed the Body of the plight of stranded OFWs in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, most of whom have abandoned their jobs due to maltreatment, violence and other abuses from their foreign employers. Stressed that it is not only a problem of uncaring and incompetent consular
officials in Saudi Arabia but also a wrong policy
made worse. Opined that the Aquino government
is just as negligent as the previous administrations because of the “infinitesimal” national budget for the DFA. Added that the reduction of the legal assistance fund (LAF) for OFWs was a gross violation of the Migrant Workers´ Act which mandates that the DFA must allot at least P100 million for the repatriation, medical assistance and other welfare services for OFWs in distress.
Appealed to the House Members not just for an investigation but an outright action to bring
home distressed Filipinos stranded in Jeddah.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2011-02-07

rows.author: F118
rows.title_full: HARASSMENT AND MURDER COMMITTED BY THE CPP-NPA-NDF
rows.abstract:
Noted the alarming incidents of harassments, intimidations and murders of the Filipino
people by the CPP-NPA-NDF). Observed acts of murder and economic sabotage committed as well as the setting up of illegal checkpoints throughout the country. Lamented that no Member has mustered enough courage to raise the issue and make a stinging condemnation of these terrorists. Called on the members of Bayan Muna, Gabriela and Anakpawis, among others, to tell their comrades to stop their outrageous
acts against humanity. Appealed that his resolutions re: protection of human life and
preservation of freedom be acted upon. Asked his colleagues to unite to effectively destroy godlessness, inhumanity and violence.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2011-02-15

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: ON THE DEATH OF FORMER AFP CHIEF OF STAFF AND CABINET SECRETARY ANGELO REYES
rows.title_short: Death Of Retired General Angelo T. Reyes
rows.abstract:
Reminisced why the death of Gen. Angelo Reyes was an irreparable loss to the country and described him as a decisive, courageous, dedicated and multi-awarded leader; a sincere and determined official who cared about the common soldier; one who constantly strove to reach his goals amidst success and failure; and a warrior who was always ready, willing and able to lay down his life to defend peace. Rued the fact that verbal savagery killed Sec. Reyes and ruined his reputation and opined that mutual respect and civility should have accompanied
the quest for truth, propriety and balance.
Read a statement from the general´s family entitled, “Angie: The Real Thing”. Thanked the sons of Gen. Reyes for sharing their father with his countrymen and read a poem as a tribute to the departed soldier and then bid the late General goodbye.
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2011-02-15

rows.author: A007
rows.title_full: VALENTINE'S DAY CELEBRATION AND TRIBUTE TO THE LATE SECRETARY ANGELO REYES
rows.title_short: Love, Valentine's Day And Angie Reyes
rows.abstract:
Stated that it might be appropriate to reflect beyond Valentines Day commercialized and restrictive import, for love is truly beyond chocolates and romantics, involving great
sacrifice, commitment, pain and loss as can be seen in the life and times of Ret. Gen. Angelo
“Angie” Reyes. Rued the fact that the death of Gen. Reyes has continued to spark intense debate on what drove him to take his life and lamented that even after he had offered his life, people still engaged in fingerpointing when they are all part and parcel of the problems and solutions. Averred that the work of reform must continue, but must steer from the agenda of political vindictiveness, revenge and retribution.
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2011-02-22

rows.author: E046
rows.title_full: DISTRIBUTION ON THE FLOOR OF THE PASTORAL LETTER ON THE REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH BILL
rows.title_short: C B C P Pastoral Letter Rejecting Reproductive Health Bill
rows.abstract:
Reacted to the pastoral letter recently
issued by the Catholic Bishop´s Conference of
the Phils. and asked why it was rejecting the Reproductive Health agenda. Clarified that the RH Bill also chose life and in fact prohibited abortion; Stressed that the problem lies in the CBCP´s interpretation of the beginning of life which was fertilization instead of conception. As the moral issue is drawn from the line that fertilization is the beginning of life, Rep. Marcoleta emphasized that there is no moral issue involved in the RH Bill but simply a social and economic issue as a couple would choose to delay the wife´s pregnancy because of economic expediency. Stressed that the issuance of said pastoral letter has a political consequence as it gives undue influence to the Members of Congress and has breached the separation of Church and State. Enjoined the Members to approach the issue not from the teachings of the Church as it cannot impose said teachings on non-Catholics.
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2011-02-22

rows.author: G012
rows.title_full: BATASANG PAMBANSA AS ONE OF THE \"AMAZING HOLES\" IN THE WORLD
rows.title_short: Being A Proud Member Of The House Of Representatives
rows.abstract:
Called the attention of the Body to an E-mail that gave a negative impression on the
House of Representatives. Presented said Email entitled “Five Amazing Holes in the World,” and lamented that the House was among the five holes
and was branded with a false label of “Rat Hole” capable of swallowing billions of pesos annually. Called upon the Members to take the same as a challenge to help transform the negative impression through good deeds that are worthy of public trust. Called on the people to refrain from feigning a blind eye to what the Members are doing to improve their lives as the House is the people´s embodiment of their aspirations. Stressed that the present crop of lawmakers shall usher in a fresh hope for a better future, as shown by an all-time satisfaction rating.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2011-02-22

rows.author: G107
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR THE IMMEDIATE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROGRAMS PROVIDED FOR IN THE EXPANDED SENIOR CITIZENS ACT OF 2010
rows.title_short: Senior Citizen's Privileges And Benefits Under Republic Act No. 9994
rows.abstract:
Expressed concern about the proposal of the Department of Finance to remove the 12% VAT enjoyed by senior citizens and of the DSWD to limit social monthly pensions for senior citizens to indigents 80 years old and above. Stressed that the law must be followed and
said that the basis of these benefits were the Constitution, as well as the Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 2010 or RA No. 9994, which granted various medical, financial, social, and educational benefits to senior citizens. Said that he had filed a bill defining violence against the elderly and added that the latter would not reach old age because of poverty and illness. Appealed for the implementation of law-mandated programs for senior citizens such as the establishment of special housing programs and social safety nets. Remarked that respect and
care for the elderly was a Filipino value and tradition. Stressed that the State must recognize the role of senior citizens in society by responding to their needs and that the youth must listen to the wise counsel of the aged.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2011-02-23

rows.author: G085
rows.title_full: NEED FOR STRATEGIC URBAN PLANNING
rows.abstract:
Inquired as to whether it was good to stop urban migration even if it could be done. Cited
the positive relationship between urbanization and economic growth as pointed out by experts.
Noted the fast rate of urbanization in the country despite its poor economic performance;
the country´s failure to translate said high
rate into increases in income, consumption and investment; and the uncontrollable migration to the cities. Suggested the conversion of the growing urban population into real human capital; the provision of roads from rural areas to urban centers; and citizen participation in every local government unit in steering the direction of the community. Concluded that development can be achieved only through a strong and effective leadership.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2011-02-22

rows.author: F118
rows.title_full: ON THE CEASEFIRE AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE GOVERNMENT AND THE CPP-NPA-NDF
rows.title_short: Insincerity Of Communist Rebels On Peace Negotiations With The G P H
rows.abstract:
Focused on the ceasefire agreement between the Government and the Communist Party of the Philippines-New People´s Army-National Democratic
Front as a prelude to the forthcoming peace talks. Inquired on the membership of the NDF´s Central Committee, Military Commission and National Executive Committee to ensure that they could be held responsible for any violations that the NPA might commit. Called upon the government to implement the UNs´ mode of Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration (DDR) with regard to peace negotiations. Called on Congress to immediately investigate the issues surrounding the peace talks as they need to be circumspect, precise and focused on the issues considering the suspicious character and attitude of the CPP-NPA who have a bleak and smudged track record of insincerity, inhumanity
and obsession to violence.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2011-02-22

rows.author: F115
rows.title_full: PROTECTION OF SENIOR CITIZENS AGAINST VIOLENCE AND MALTREATMENT
rows.abstract:
Spoke on the maltreatment of a senior citizen in Mandaluyong City which was seen on television nationwide. Cited Art. XIII, Sec. 11 of the
Constitution which speaks of integrated health development, availability of affordable social services and priority for the needs of the elderly; and that it is the duty of the family to take care of the elderly members while the State may design programs of social security for them. Asked how the State may intervene when the family fails in its duty to take care of the elderly or worse, when the latter are actually abused. Presented a video which was shown on national television of an elderly, Aling Anita, who was imprisoned in a steel entrapment in her own home, and maltreated by her own daughter and son-in-law. Expressed his intent to introduce
legislations that would favor senior citizens.
rows.status: Transmitted to the Committee on Appropriations on 2011-08-03
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Crisologo. Referred to the appropriate committee.

committee_action.meethigh: Approved in the Committee.  To be consolidated with HBs 1071, 2135, 2928 and 2929 and Privilege Speech No. 00179.  TWG was created to craft the final version.

committee_action.action: Transmitted to the Committee on Appropriations on 2011-08-03

rows.author: F071
rows.title_full: IMPLEMENTATION OF THE CONDITIONAL CASH TRANSFER PROGRAM
rows.title_short: Conditional Cash Transfer ( C C T )
rows.abstract:
Pointed out that in an agricultural district marked by productive and lean months such
as his, workers had been absent whenever money
was released under the Conditional Cash Transfer
(CCT) program. Opined that thus, the government
should be more flexible in implementing the program so as not to promote mendicancy and could grant money in bulk during lean months and require fathers to work all-year round. Urged the Executive Department to prove that the program was not a doleout and to find more ways to make it more effective.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2011-02-22

rows.author: G042
rows.title_full: \"FOOD CRISIS\"
rows.abstract:
Saying his province experienced a recent calamity, Rep. Evardone cited abnormal weather changes throughout the world and the looming food crisis as a result thereof. Dwelling on the Philippine situation, he said that food importation was no longer an option because the period of cheap and abundant food supplies
in the global market was gone. He suggested
that the government immediately pass a coherent, adequately-funded and science-based agenda for food sufficiency and in the meantime, forge a public-private partnership for an intensified food production program.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOOD SECURITY since 2011-02-22

rows.author: F086
rows.title_full: ON CONGRESS LOSING THE SO-CALLED \"POWER OF THE PURSE\"
rows.title_short: Authority Of Congress To Legislate Budget Every Year
rows.abstract:
Spoke on the power of Congress to undertake its constitutionally mandated duty of enacting the General Appropriations Bill every year. Pointed out an alleged “error” in the implementation of the “power” of the Legislative Department over the purse that has “remained unabated and has emasculated Congress with possible consequences to the State and the people.” Maintained that the “power” of Congress over the purse...provide a system of check and balance on the discretionary powers of the Executive Department regarding its use of public appropriations. Delved on the transferring of funds...and as to how the power of the purse has been significantly diminished through the years. 
Added that currently, there is a great imbalance in the power of the purse with the Executive Branch able to override the mandate of the legislature through the GAA. Said that savings could be used for discretionary, intelligence, and other purposes which the legislative officially had no oversight about. Pointed out that the President´s impoundment or refusal to release funds appropriated by Congress was another budget control mechanism. Stressed that Congress must retrieve its constitutional power of the purse as a coequal branch and asked his colleagues to support bills he had filed in this regard.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2011-03-01

rows.author: F035
rows.title_full: INTERNATIONAL DAY FOR THE MOTHER LANGUAGE
rows.abstract:
Reminded the Body that it was “Int'l Mother Language Day,” a UNESCO proclamation to encourage people to maintain their use of the mother language as well as to learn other
languages inasmuch as language was a unique source of meaning for understanding, writing and expressing reality. Stressed that illiteracy was one major obstacle to nation-building and sustainable development... and opined that the inability of Filipino students to understand the language of instruction resulted in poor comprehension skills and below-passing test scores as shown in surveys. Explained that Trends in Int'l Mathematics and Science Study provides reliable and timely data on students´ achievements all over the world and  noted that 1) most Filipino high school students fail to answer simple questions ....; 2) said students perform better when tests are written in their native language, as proven by the experiment conducted by the DepEd ...; 3) the use of the mother tongue in education does not hinder the learning of the English language; and 4) the time for learning a second language like English will not improve the students´ competence therein. Urged the DepEd to pursue the mother tongue-based multilingual education under
the K+12 program and allow the country to accomplish its targets under the MDGs and Education for All.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2011-03-01
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Padilla. Referred to Rules.

rows.author: F118
rows.title_full: ON THE NEWS BLACKOUT ON THE ONGOING PEACE NEGOTIATIONS
rows.title_short: Closed - Door Peace Negotiation Is Oslo, Norway.
rows.abstract:
Pointed out several concerns surrounding the end of the first round of formal peace negotiations between the Communist Party of the Phils.-New People´s Army (CPP-NPA) and the government, among which were: 1) the government´s position and transparency in dealing with the peace process; and 2) the highly questionable admission by Office of the Presidential Adviser on the Peace Process (OPAPP)Sec.Teresita  “Ging” Deles that the government was wrong in using force and arms to quell insurgency. Relayed ANAD´s belief that despite the peace negotiations, the government security forces
should continue to perform their regulation function and allow the rule of law to prevail without need of sacrificing the desire to negotiate political expediency out of the peace process. Lamented that the Resolutions he filed have not been acted upon, and called on his colleagues to join him in seeking out the truth in the spirit of President Aquino´s call for transparency and honesty.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2011-03-01
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Cagas. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G068
rows.title_full: ON FILIPINOS WITH PENDING CASES IN FOREIGN COUNTRIES
rows.title_short: Sentiment Of Filipinos Awaiting Trial In Foreign Countries
rows.abstract:
Expressed his personal sentiment in solidarity with Rep. Ronald V. Singson who is awaiting
his fate in Hong Kong for a drug trafficking offense, and with other hundreds of Filipinos under similar circumstances abroad. Said that Rep. Singson deserves the same attention given by the government and the Filipino people over the tragedy of Flor Contemplacion, Alma Concepcion and Nora Aunor for drug-related offenses, among others. Suggested that the
Members exercise an act of camaraderie for a peer in distress in a foreign land. He concluded that Rep. Singson should not be deprived of the opportunity to prove himself worthy of the trust and respect of his constituents by allowing them to decide whether he is still deserving of their mandate in 2013.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2011-03-01

rows.author: G057
rows.title_full: STRESSED THE IMPORTANCE OF THE PARTICIPATION OF MINDANAO CONGRESSMEN IN THE ONGOING JOINT MEETING OF THE COMMITTES ON SUFFRAGE AND MUSLIM AFFAIRS ON THE ARMM ELECTION POSTPONEMENT
rows.title_short: Autonomous Region Of Muslim Mindanao ( A R M M ) Election
rows.abstract:
Took the floor to explain what transpired
during the hearing of the Cttees. on Muslim
Affairs and Suffrage and Election Reforms. Referred to Rep. Acmad M. Tomawis´ motion to allow the Members representing the Muslims to go to their respective districts and consult with their people but that said motion, was not acted upon by the Joint Committee, and for which reason the Muslim members thereof decided not to participate in the voting process. Emphasized that they belong to the coalition and support the Administration, but that they would like things to be done in accordance with their
constitutional mandate, particularly in matters of consulting with the people the destiny of their Muslim brothers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2011-03-01
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: C045
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR THE FILING OF IMPEACHMENT COMPLAINT AGAINST THE SUPREME COURT JUSTICES WHO VOTED HASTILY ON THE ISSUANCE OF A STATUS QUO ANTE ON THE IMPEACHMENT CASE AGAINST OMBUSMAN GUTIERREZ AS THIS AMOUNTS TO BETRAYAL OF PUBLIC TRUST.
rows.abstract:
Rep. Fariñas said that he would have risen initially to thank the Supreme Court for seeing the light of his arguments that the House can handle the multiple complaints filed against an impeachable officer, and that simultaneous referral of several complaints to the Committee on Justice is allowed. However, he said that he was startled by the decision of the Court, esp. the concurring opinion of Justice Antonio Carpio - that the Supreme Court, without even allowing its members to read the petition
of Ombudsman Merceditas Gutierrez asking the
Supreme Court to nullify the proceedings of the
House, and for the issuance of restraining order
against it, voted against the objection of three
members who invoked that they should be given the
opportunity to read the petition. He said that it was unfortunate that the Court decided to issue a status quo ante order against the House.
Said order, he maintained, was issued but was lifted by the Court with the position that the acts of the House are constitutional. He opined that the House should therefore allow the proceedings to reach its finality. After explaining that the Committee voted to give Ombudsman Gutierrez the remaining period she
had to submit her answer, and that failure on her part to do so would mean proceeding with the impeachment hearings, Rep. Fariñas appealed to
his colleagues to look into the actuations of the
Court. He underscored that it is the people who can take away from those in office the privilege to serve. Rep. Fariñas pointed out that whenever the representatives of the people feel that they have betrayed public trust, these officials can be removed from office by impeachment. Expressed belief that the members of the Supreme Court who voted to issue a status quo ante order against the House without even reading the petition have violated the public trust. He informed the Body that he will soon review the matter and initiate impeachment proceedings against them and appealed to the Supreme Court to leave the records of their proceedings intact so that the Members can find out who among them voted to issue the status quo ante order without having received the copy of the petition by Ombudsman Gutierrez.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2011-03-01
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G025
rows.title_full: ON THE PHILIPPINES HAVING THE HIGHEST POWER RATES IN THE WORLD
rows.abstract:
Rep. Cojuangco expressed concern about recent
news reports that the Philippines had the highest
power rates in the world. Stressed that House Bill No. 1291 which would re-open the Bataan Nuclear Power Plant was the only solution to the power crisis. She thus urged the coauthors of said Bill and the rest of the Body to start deliberating on the measure .
rows.status: Referred to stakeholders on 2011-03-07

rows.manual_status: Committee Report No. 2010, together with HR No. 935
rows.author: A027
rows.title_full: THE CIRCUMSTANCES SURROUNDING THE DEPORTATION OF THE 14 TAIWANESE INDIVIDUALS TO THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF CHINA NECESSITATING A REVIEW OF THE PHILIPPINES ONE CHINE POLICY (CALLED FOR THE REVIEW OF THE PHILIPPINES \"ONE CHINA POLICY\")
rows.title_short: Deportation Of Taiwanese Nationals To China.
rows.abstract:
Rep. Diaz talked about the gross anomaly committed by the Bureau of Immigration
and Deportation (BID) and the Department of Justice (DOJ) in deporting 14 Taiwanese nationals to China. He stated that these Taiwanese nationals were claimed as “undocumented
aliens” even though the Taipei Economic and
Cultural Office (TECO) had presented documents
proving otherwise. He pointed out that OFWs in Taiwan are now being affected by the strict rules of the Taiwanese Government as a repercussion of said deportation. As he stressed that the Phil. government should have deported all the 14 Taiwanese nationals ... Rep. Diaz lamented the gross violation committed by the BID and DOJ. He disclosed his request for an intensified review of the investigation being presently undertaken and cautioned that the country has a bilateral trade agreement with Taiwan amounting to $6 million and that it is expecting the arrival of some 200,000 Taiwanese tourists.
rows.status: Committee Report on Adopted Measure Pending with Rules since 2012-03-13
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Congressman Cagas. Referred to  the Committee on Rules. Committee Report No. 2010, together with HR No. 935

second_reading.comm_report_action: Informing the House of its findings and recommendations

rows.author: F103
rows.title_full: ON THE COUNTRY'S AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES INDUSTRY
rows.abstract:
Emphasized that the government, should also pay
attention to rice production as well as local livestock and poultry industries if only to achieve food sufficiency for its growing population. Referred to the recent agriculture and fisheries summit in Antipolo City wherein Agriculture Sec. Proceso Alcala reminded
the participants to take note of the reality that
poverty is largely agricultural, and that the price of food is dependent on agricultural productivity. Enjoined his colleagues, to contribute to the development of the agriculture and fisheries sectors by: stopping smuggling activities on agricultural products and other
commodities through responsive and stringent
anti-smuggling measures; strengthening and creating institutions that provide credit assistance to small farmers and producers; and creating a dynamic fiscal policy that would push the agriculture and fishery sectors a notch higher if not the highest from where it is at the moment in the order of government´s fiscal
and development priorities. Summoned the collective will of the Body to focus on the things that must be done in the pursuit of agriculture and fisheries development.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND FISHERIES since 2011-02-23
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Apostol.  Referred to Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F104
rows.title_short: Teaching The Young Filipinos On E D S A People Power.
rows.abstract:
Rep. Palatino talked about the coming 25th anniversary of the EDSA People Power Revolution and paid tribute to the millions of Filipinos who valiantly fought for democracy during the dark days of Martial Law. He expressed concern however that said event has lost its relevance especially to the youth as they have little or almost no knowledge of the 1986 People Power. He stressed that the legacy of the EDSA People Power is too important especially for the
masses who yearn for freedom, justice and peace and should not be monopolized by politicians and bureaucrats. Thereupon, Rep. Palatino urged the youth to join the celebration by pledging to serve the people and demand for genuine change, freedom and pro-people governance as EDSA´s promises of change remain unfulfilled.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2011-02-23
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G099
rows.title_full: ON DEMEANING OF WOMEN IN MEDIA
rows.title_short: Discriminatory Portrayal Of Women In Media
rows.abstract:
Delved on the exploitation of female sexuality and the portrayal of women in a discriminatory,
demeaning and derogatory manner in advertising. Stated that per the United Nations, advertising is the worst offender in perpetuating the image of women as sex symbols and an inferior class
of human beings and expressed apprehension that
mediums like the Internet are deliberately crossing the line and straining the standards on self-regulation in the portrayal of women. Enjoined the Members, particularly the Lady Legislators, to look into ways of upholding the dignity of women particularly their portrayal in advertising.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2011-05-10

rows.author: G078
rows.title_full: ON HIV/AIDS AWARENESS
rows.title_short: H I V / A I D S Human Immuno Virus / Acute Immune Deficiency Syndrome
rows.abstract:
Spoke on the ill-effects of human immuno
deficiency virus-acquired immune deficiency syndrome (HIV-AIDS), and cited figures from the DOH on the increasing number of recorded cases of fullblown infection, particularly among the young people. Focused on 1) the expensive cost of
treating patients; 2) the need to conduct HIV-AIDS test; and 3) the issue of discrimination and marginalization to people who are already suffering from the disease. Stressed the need to prevent and address the spread of the disease, and recommended measures such as the provision of formal education to children, whom she emphasized would become the country´s future leaders and movers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2011-05-10

rows.author: F113
rows.title_full: ON WOMEN IN POLITICS
rows.abstract:
Congratulated all the women legislators from the past up to the present for being part of the legislative process,... Delved on the involvement of Filipino women in politics and lawmaking beginning from the enactment into law of Act No. 4112 up to the establishment of the First Congress in 1946 and claimed that up to the existing 15th Congress, 320 women legislators had been elected to the Lower
House and 17 into the Senate. Maintained that
the participation of women legislators in lawmaking is essential in the enactment of laws concerning women, children and their families.
Paid tribute not only to the late former Pres. Corazon C. Aquino for being an icon of Filipino democracy and for being the first woman-President; and former President and first woman-Vice-President and now Representative Gloria M. Macapagal-Arroyo, for her contributions to the economic well-being of the country, but also to the many women local officials.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2011-05-10

rows.author: F093
rows.title_full: ON WOMEN'S APPEAL FOR A JUST AND LASTING PEACE
rows.abstract:
Discussed what peace meant for many Filipino women who are at the forefront of battles
against poverty, war and violence; equal rights
and social injustice; unemployment and loss of livelihood, and human rights violations. Underscored that it is the impact of armed conflicts and of the military´s counterinsurgency program and civilian military
operations that have far-reaching and damaging
consequences to women and their families.
Claimed that the resumption of peace talks between the Government and the National Democratic Front; the exploratory peace talks between the GRP and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), while laudable, must only be achieved by addressing the root causes of the armed conflict - poverty, social injustice, landlessness and human rights violations. Urged her colleagues to support all efforts for peace and called for an investigation on the
harassment of women in the Third District of Davao City by uniformed men.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2011-05-10

rows.author: F069
rows.title_full: ON \"KABABAIHANG INIWAN NG ASAWA AT KABABAIHANG NANG-IWAN NG ASAWA\"
rows.abstract:
Rose on behalf of single or solo parents raising the modern Filipino family, citing the rising incidents of marital separation as one of its causes. Identified who the solo parents are under
the Solo Parents Act and opined that women as
solo parents are a more imposing problem and challenge. Also forwarded the cause of the laudable efforts of the State and the steps they were taking towards the full support and promotion of modern families. Urged her colleagues to be proactive and sensitive to the circumstances of their constituents, become their advocates and deafening voices for a better society, forwarding the cause of the
young as they forward now the cause of the mother, the woman.
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2011-05-10

rows.author: G025
rows.title_full: ON MORATORIUM TO THE BATAAN NUCLEAR POWER PLANT
rows.abstract:
Initially expressed her deepest sympathy to all the people of Fukushima, Sendai in Japan, who were greatly affected by the tsunami and the explosion of one of its nuclear power plant as a
result of the 8.9 magnitude earthquake that hit Japan last March 11, 2011. Declared that she was imposing upon herself a temporary moratorium in pushing for the discussion of HB No. 1291 and their advocacy until all the facts on the safety of nuclear power are cleared. Maintained that Fukushima was not Chernobyl and that it would never be it because of its containment structures but averred that should it fail, then she would immediately withdraw the Bill and their advocacy. Also rued the fact that the Philippines could have lost the only viable alternative to fossil power which is cheap, safe and reliable and urged the Members to understand first the issue well, to wait for the facts
and to debate before they decide.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2011-05-10

rows.author: G031
rows.title_full: ON OFW MOTHERS WHO LEFT THEIR FAMILIES BEHIND
rows.abstract:
Took the floor to honor and pay tribute to all the overseas Filipina workers, particularly the OFW mothers who have to bear the painful burden of leaving their husbands and children behind in order to provide better lives for them; they who toil unceasingly and endured discrimination simply because they are Filipina, yet bear their anguish with decency and dignity and they who were hailed as living heroes for keeping the Philippines afloat in tumultuous times like the 1997 Asian financial crisis and the recent global recession. Expressed hope that together
with the Aquino administration, they can combine
and coordinate efforts to ensure the esteem and
protection not only of OFWs but also, to bestow better opportunities for women in the Philippines as well.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2011-05-10

rows.author: G086
rows.title_full: ON PEACE IN THE ARMM
rows.title_short: Women In Politics / Autonomous Region In Muslim Mindanao ( A R M M ) Reforms
rows.abstract:
Paid tribute to her fellow women legislators
who have contributed to the advancement of
women´s rights in the Philippines. In celebration
of the International Women´s Month, she then
opted to expound on what the Moro women clamor
for: to live a peaceful, prosperous life, free from the torments of war and displacement. This as she said that everytime war rages in their homeland, it is the women, children and elderly who suffered the widowing and impoverishing effects of war. Proposed to revisit the 1996 MNLFGRP Final Peace Agreement, to end the centuries-old problem and make it acceptable to the MILF who are still in an uncertain peace talk with the Philippine government. Also stated that she took the initiative of reforming the ARMM by filing HB No.4146 and urged her colleagues to support this laborious but inevitable and correct direction.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2011-05-10

rows.author: G103
rows.title_full: ON WOMEN IN AGRICULTURE
rows.abstract:
Cited the UN Millennium Declaration of 2000 and UN Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW) in discussing the work situation of rural
women who constituted almost a quarter of all women workers in the country. Asked Congress to address their socio-economic and political concerns such as their role as beneficiaries of agrarian reform, participation in governance, and access to comprehensive health. Reminded her colleagues that illiteracy, lack of employment and ill health were more prevalent in the rural areas, and stressed the need for responsive policies and programs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 2011-05-10

rows.author: G105
rows.title_full: ON WOMEN IN SOCIAL SERVICES
rows.abstract:
Said that the plight of Filipino women had been exacerbated by liberalization, privatization, and deregulation. Discussed the statistics on rising costs of goods and services; poor health, educational, and employment opportunities; and inadequate family incomes. Asked for more direction-oriented, propeople, and dignifying government programs; and for a propoor,
compassionate, and responsive administration that
was serious about implementing genuine land reform and doing away with neo-liberal policies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POVERTY ALLEVIATION since 2011-05-24

rows.author: F084
rows.title_full: ON DEPRESSION AS AN ILLNESS NOT A CHOICE
rows.abstract:
Cited local and international facts and statistics on depression which she referred
to as a much-maligned and misunderstood illness
leading to suicide and death. Explained that the
same was highly treatable if diagnosed early and provided with societal support. Proposed an integrated approach to the problem by allocating enough resources and coordinating agency efforts as well as training health care providers concerned.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2011-03-14)

rows.author: F096
rows.title_full: ON WOMEN IN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES
rows.title_short: Indigenous Women As The Poorest Of The Poor
rows.abstract:
Talked about the plight of indigenous peoples, particularly the indigenous women who remain to be the poorest, most violated, most oppressed, most scorned and the most exploited sector
in society. Pointed out that the government
has failed to address their basic social needs, and that they continue to suffer from poor health services and other basic needs of sustaining life that led them to turn into beggars and prostitutes in order to sustain
their family´s needs. Commended and acknowledged the indigenous women in the country as they continue to be at the forefront in fighting for their family´s survival among which is the inspiring and success story of Ms. Analyn Aryo, a nanny who hails from an indigenous tribe but through perseverance became an author of the book “Nanny Tales.” Enjoined the Members to pledge and commit themselves in promoting the welfare and advancement of the indigenous women.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2011-05-10

rows.author: G081
rows.title_full: ON OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES TO PEACE AND DEVELOPMENT
rows.abstract:
In celebration of International Women´s Month
and World Water Day, Rep. Sahidulla spoke on the
social, economic and political challenges besetting Mindanao, particularly its quests for peace and development and of giving new voice and hope to Mindanao women. She stressed that instead of bullets and mortar, the women of Mindanao had embraced sisterhood and had rediscovered their important role and influence in civil and political matters. She thereafter focused on other Mindanao issues like the need for potable water, peace and development and participation in a free and fair election and
sought the support of Congress and the Filipinos in the attainment of peace and development in Mindanao.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2011-05-10

rows.author: G106
rows.title_full: ON HER CALL TO SUPPORT AND PROMOTE WOMEN'S RIGHTS
rows.title_short: Legislations Promoting Women's Rights And Welfare
rows.abstract:
Stressed the significance of March 8 for all the women in the world, because it marks the centennial commemoration of International
Women´s Day. Traced the history of the battles fought by women´s rights advocates, and
emphasized the role of Filipino women legislators in pursuing and supporting their rights and role in society. Urged her fellow female legislators and Filipino women in general to remain vigilant in supporting and advancing women´s rights in the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2011-05-10

rows.title_full: RESPONDED TO NEWS ARTICLE STATING THAT MISAMIS ORIENTAL IS ONE OF THE MOST UNSAFE PLACES IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Took the floor to refute the inclusion of the Province of Misamis Oriental among the eight provinces identified as unsafe based on a survey allegedly conducted by the Phil. Information Agency, which appeared in the March 13, 2011 issue of the Philippine Daily Inquirer. Personally vouched for the peace and order situation in said province which was very near his Province of Camiguin and thereafter
questioned the methodology and sampling used
in the survey. Cited the negative implications
of the news article and urged media practitioners to practice responsible journalism so as not to thwart potential tourists and investors from visiting Northern Mindanao.  Stressed that critical data should be validated and members of the media should strive to balance their reporting of information because they are a potent tool in the decisionmaking process as well as in public information.
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2011-05-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Dimaporo (F). Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G041
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR SUPPORT FOR JAPAN AFTER THE MARCH 11, 2011 EARTHQUAKE AND TSUNAMI
rows.title_short: Sympathy And Support To The People Of Japan
rows.abstract:
Expressed sympathy for Japan which has hit by an
earthquake, tsunami and nuclear fallout. Expressed support to giving assistance to Japan with the hope of a faster recovery and strength to cope with the aftermath of the tragedy. 
Stated that he had filed House Resolution No. 1088 expressing the House´s deepest sympathy and support to the government and people of Japan and
urged his colleagues to express the same.
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2011-05-10

rows.title_full: ON THE PHILIPPINES' DISASTER PREPAREDNESS
rows.abstract:
Spoke on a matter of urgency and importance to the nation - preparedness for disaster similar to what happened in Japan. Given the catastrophic events, Rep. Valencia inquired
whether the Filipinos are ready for the big one
and what steps have been taken for any eventuality. Urgently called for a special
meeting with all concerned government and private
agencies as to what safety measures have been undertaken in the event that such calamities would take place.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2011-05-10

rows.author: G093
rows.title_full: ON THE DEMAND OF TEACHERS FOR DECENT COMPENSATION
rows.title_short: Salary Increase Of Public School Teachers
rows.abstract:
Spoke on the demand of public school teachers for decent compensation. Informed the Body that hundreds of public school teachers marched to Congress to demand for the approval of House Bill No. 2142 or the Salary Upgrading Bill for Public School Teachers which he filed and which seeks to increase the salaries of public school teachers to Salary Grade 15. Then called
for the immediate passage of said measure.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2011-05-10

rows.author: F059
rows.title_full: ON HONORING THE FILIPINO VETERANS OF WWII IN COMMEMORATION OF THE 69TH ANNIVERSARY OF \"ARAW NG KAGITINGAN\"
rows.abstract:
Talked about the plight of World War II veterans
as they commemorate the 69th anniversary of
Araw ng Kagitingan on April 9, 2011. Recalled what happened in Corregidor and its neighboring towns during WWII. Cited stories about the heroism and courage of several veterans. Lamented the fact that provisions
of the Constitution and RA No. 6948 on
the protection and promotion of the rights of veterans and their families, were being undermined by the nonpayment of veterans benefits such as the old-age monthly pension under RA No. 6948 and the additional disability pension under RA No. 7696. Urged the government to promptly and completely give what was due these unsung heroes while their living and health expenses continued to rise; and expressed hope that the Senate would act on her House-approved Bill increasing burial assistance for veterans.
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2011-05-10
rows.remarks: Manifestations of Reps. Mercado-Revilla and Bataoil. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F034
rows.title_full: ON THE NEED TO STRENGTHEN THE COUNTRY'S DISASTER PREPAREDNESS PROGRAM
rows.abstract:
Advanced several engineering interventions to address the issue of weak buildings which might not be able to withstand strong earthquakes. Proposed the following:
1) a structural audit of public infrastructures
should be conducted to identify those that require seismic retrofitting; 2) government agencies should include in their respective budgets the amounts necessary for the structural audit and retrofitting; 3) the present Engineering curricula should be reviewed
so as to include the subjects of Earthquake
Engineering and Structural Engineering
among those required; and 4) Congress should
consider enacting a Building Code that would
address the structural designs of low-cost houses.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2011-03-22
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: C045
rows.title_full: ON THE PARAMETERS TO BE USED BY THE HOUSE IN FUTURE IMPEACHMENT CASES IN VIEW OF THE RESIGNATION OF OMBUDSMAN MERCEDITAS GUTIERREZ
rows.title_short: Resignation Of Former Ombudsman Merceditas Gutierrez.
rows.abstract:
Focused on the matter of the impeachment of former Ombudsman Merceditas Gutierrez. Thanked Ms. Gutierrez for resigning and wished that she had resigned earlier so she could have saved the House from the time and effort of preparing for the trial. Thereafter read before the Body a Memorandum about the letter of Exec. Sec. Paquito Ochoa Jr., transmitting to Congress a copy of the resignation letter for appropriate action by the House. Stated that in view of latest development, the impeachment trial
had become moot and academic. However maintained that the Committee on Justice by itself cannot declare the case moot and academic, and that the case should be tackled by the Body in plenary session because the complainant is the House itself. Stressed that it is the House and not merely the Committee on Justice that should adopt a resolution, unless the House gives full authority to the latter to take up the issue on the floor. Emphasized that the degree of
accountability that the House required of the
Ombudsman should also be the same parameter
that it should use for all other impeachable officers. Quoted the words of Minority Leader
Edcel C. Lagman that in the case of Ms. Gutierrez, she was not guilty of graft and corruption, but that she failed to act promptly on the cases filed in the Office of the Ombudsman.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2011-05-17
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Escudero. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G122
rows.title_full: ON THE ENVIRONMENTAL PROBLEMS OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Spoke about the negative impact of capitalism and consumerism on the environment even as the country has enough laws to prevent illegal logging and deforestation. Appealed to the Members to allow environment advocates and NGOs
adequate opportunities and freedom to promote
environmental preservation. Applauded the Members who had filed pro-environment bills and expressed hope that HB No. 6796 which sought to ban illegal logging in Mindanao, would be passed into law and properly implemented. Pleaded to the Body to do everything within their means to protect the environment while they still have the mandate to do so.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2011-05-17

rows.author: E022
rows.title_full: ON THE RESIGNATION OF OMBUDSMAN MERCEDITAS GUTIERREZ
rows.title_short: Resignation Of Former Ombudsman Merceditas Gutierrez
rows.abstract:
Underscored that the sudden resignation of Ombudsman Merceditas Gutierrez 10 days before her impeachment trial in the Senate had derailed the efforts to curb corruption in government and remove the alleged formidable stumbling block to making former Pres. Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo and her officials accountable for their crimes. Maintained that the impeachment trial of Ombudsman Gutierrez would have further exposed the gross inexcusable delays and inaction on cases involving the previous Administration as well as the accountabilities of the former president. Cited in particular, Ombudsman Gutierrez´ deleterious action on Task Force Abono which the Ombudsman´s field investigation office had created to investigate the so-called GMA fertilizer fund scam. Maintained that Ombudsman Gutierrez deserves to be charged with criminal and administrative cases not only for her inactions but also for derailing all investigative work of Task Force Abono. Proposed that the House Committee on Justice provide assistance to initiatives to pursue such criminal and administrative cases against Ombudsman Gutierrez and to conduct a legislative inquiry on how her actionshad resulted to the derailment of the investigation of the fertilizer fund scam. Further underscored
the importance of making the alleged beneficiary
of the Ombudsman´s action, former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo, accountable
for her past deeds.
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2011-05-17

rows.author: F016
rows.title_full: ON THE PHILIPPINE JUVENILE JUSTICE SYSTEM
rows.abstract: Spoke mainly on the increasing involvement of the youth in criminal activities and the need for government authorities to address this problem by amending RA No.9344 or the Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act of 2006, especially with respect to the weaknesses of the law which criminal syndicates and sometimes, parents themselves take advantage of to further their illegal activities and her goal in filing House Bill No. 2611 Re: RESTORING THE CRIMINAL RESPONSIBILITY OF CHILDREN UNDER 18 YEARS OF AGE. Expressed satisfaction that the Committee on Revision of Laws had already adopted and approved a substitute version on the matter. Sought for the immediate passage of said Bill to promote the interest of the people for an orderly society.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2011-05-17

rows.author: E012
rows.title_full: UTILIZATION OF RENEWABLE ENERGY RESOURCES
rows.abstract:
Spoke on the topic of renewable energy and other energy resources in light of finding solutions to deal with the global effects of climate
change. Noted that despite the passage of RA No. 9513 or the Renewable Energy Act of
2008, the country has still been beset by increasing world fuel prices and stressed that the obstacles to the full implementation of the law would depend on the National Renewable Energy Board and the Energy Regulatory Commission. Discussed about the feed-in tariff (FIT) rates for biomass energy and pointed out the need to investigate the implementation of the Renewable Energy Act as well as the composition of the NREB.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2011-05-17
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Cojuangco (K.). Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: E047
rows.title_full: WORKERS' CALL FOR WAGE INCREASE AND LOWERING OF PRICES OF COMMODITIES
rows.abstract:
Spoke about the need to increase the basic salary of workers in light of the high prices of basic commodities, services and other petroleum products as a result of the government´s
policies of liberalization, privatization and deregulation and several anti-wage laws and policies. Stressed that wage increases were not
enough in the past and noted that to date,
the Aquino Administration has not yet acted on the workers´ request for wage increase. Further claimed that the increase in toll fees, water and electricity rates and prices of basic
food commodities requires a corresponding increase in the daily basic wages of the workers.
Underscored that said increase can be justified by the billions in revenues and profits of big businesses and top corporations. Reminded the various wage board councils, employers and the government that an increase in the wages of the workers should be commensurate to what the workers and their families need. Expressed the hope that the Members of Congress would support the proposed measure legislating a wage increase.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2011-05-17
